overview.mechanism: Inhibits renal SGLT2-mediated glucose reabsorption and increases urinary glucose excretion.
uses: Investigated for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes; consult the local product insert for approved renal eligibility.

paragraphs.text: In a 21-patient pharmacokinetic study, systemic exposure was broadly similar across renal-function groups, but urinary glucose excretion declined as renal function fell. Similar exposure is not proof of preserved glucose-lowering efficacy or a dosing recommendation for severe CKD.

A pooled analysis of two 24-week trials examined glucose lowering in normal or mildly reduced eGFR. It did not establish prevention of dialysis, cardiovascular events or mortality, and should not be treated as a dedicated CKD-outcome trial.

sources.citation: Jeong et al. The effect of renal function on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of enavogliflozin in type 2 diabetes. Diabetes Obes Metab. 2024;26:2588–2597. PubMed PMID: 38618974.
Efficacy and safety of enavogliflozin vs. dapagliflozin as add-on therapy based on renal function: a pooled analysis of two randomized controlled trials. PubMed PMID: 38360626.
